query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Increasing combustion gas pressure and optimizing the nozzle design on the HVAF-i7 torch will increase the particle velocity, thereby enhancing particle kinetic energy which leads to improved splat formation and deposition efficiency, resulting in thicker and better-adherent FeCoNiCrAl coatings while maintaining oxidation resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock (15–45 μm) currently producing acceptable quality but insufficient thickness when sprayed with the standard HVAF-i7 settings.
generation.intervention: Adjust the HVAF-i7 torch by increasing the combustion gas pressure and refining the nozzle design to boost particle velocity.
generation.conditions: Operate the HVAF-i7 under modified gas flow conditions with increased combustion gas pressure and a nozzle design that enables higher particle velocity; maintain a spray distance in the range of 300–350 mm and standard substrate preheat conditions used for high-temperature thermal barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced kinetic energy of particles on impact.
generation.mechanism: By increasing particle velocity, the FeCoNiCrAl particles acquire more kinetic energy, which promotes better splat formation and adhesion upon impact. This improved deformation and bonding are expected to yield a denser, thicker coat with minimal oxidation during deposition.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in as-sprayed coating thickness and deposition efficiency compared to the baseline, while maintaining coating adhesion and oxidation resistance required for high-temperature service.
generation.baseline: Standard HVAF-i7 processing using 15–45 μm feedstock at current gas pressures and nozzle configurations, which yields acceptable coating quality but inadequate thickness.
generation.boundary: This intervention should remain effective under spray conditions with a targeted distance of 300–350 mm and within the typical substrate preheat settings for high-temperature thermal barrier applications; effectiveness may be limited if excessive particle overheating or oxidation occurs due to over-adjustment of gas pressure.
generation.uncertainty: The precise increase in gas pressure required to achieve the desired particle velocity without inducing excessive oxidation or thermal degradation is uncertain and may require iterative tuning.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform a series of controlled deposition experiments comparing the standard HVAF-i7 process to a modified process with increased gas pressure and an optimized nozzle design. Use a constant feedstock size (15–45 μm) and target spray distance (300–350 mm) while measuring coating thickness, adhesion, and oxidation levels on substrates including internal diameters of 120 mm.
measurements: Oxidation level (via microstructural or spectroscopic analysis)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the modified process does not yield a statistically significant increase in coating thickness and/or if the coatings exhibit degraded adhesion or increased oxidation compared to the baseline process, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

proposals.intervention: Increase the particle velocity via adjustment of combustion gas pressure and nozzle design on the HVAF-i7 torch
proposals.conditions: Operate the HVAF-i7 with a modified gas flow configuration and increased combustion gas pressure while targeting an optimal spray distance of ~300–350 mm; maintain standard substrate preheat conditions used in high-temperature TBC service.
proposals.structural_mediator: Enhanced kinetic energy of particles arriving at the substrate
proposals.mechanism: Higher particle velocity increases particle flattening and splat formation upon impact, thereby boosting deposition efficiency. By emulating conditions from the conventional MCrAlY studies that reported gains at higher velocities and nozzle-specific distances, the intervention is expected to yield thicker, better-adherent coatings with minimal oxidation.
proposals.predicted_outcome: An increase in as-sprayed coating thickness and deposition rate relative to the baseline (15–45 μm feedstock at standard HVAF-i7 settings) while retaining the integrity and oxidation resistance required for thermal-barrier service even in narrow internal diameters (down to 120 mm).
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This approach directly tackles the thickness limitation by increasing the kinetic energy of the feedstock particles, which, as demonstrated in prior MCrAlY work with higher particle velocity, should result in a thicker bond coat while preserving adhesion and oxidation resistance.

proposals.intervention: Optimize the spray distance to a nozzle-specific range (300–350 mm) on the HVAF-i7 torch
proposals.conditions: Adjust the torch positioning so that deposition occurs at a distance of 300–350 mm from the substrate while keeping other variables constant (15–45 μm feedstock and standard gas parameters) during deposition onto substrates mimicking internal surfaces with diameters as small as 120 mm.
proposals.structural_mediator: Adjusted impact momentum and particle dwell time in the thermal jet
proposals.mechanism: A longer, optimized spray distance enhances particle residence time within the accelerating gas jet, improving particle heating and velocity, leading to better splat formation and intersplat bonding. This replicates the slight gains in deposition efficiency observed in conventional MCrAlY studies, thus mitigating the thickness shortfall encountered with the HVAF-i7 torch.
proposals.predicted_outcome: A measurable increase in coating thickness and deposition efficiency compared to the baseline, with the thicker bond coat maintaining minimal oxidation and robust adhesion under high-temperature service conditions.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By targeting the nozzle–substrate distance shown to be optimal in prior studies, this single intervention leverages a known favorable condition (300–350 mm) to boost deposition efficiency specifically addressing the thickness challenge.

proposals.intervention: Redesign the HVAF-i7 nozzle to integrate a secondary gas acceleration stage (post-nozzle gas injection)
proposals.conditions: Implement a modified nozzle design that introduces an auxiliary high-velocity post-nozzle gas stream; operate under the revised HVAF-i7 torch settings with a spray distance of ~300 mm and standard 15–45 μm feedstock while depositing on substrates representative of internal diameters ~120 mm.
proposals.structural_mediator: Amplified particle acceleration in the exit region of the nozzle
proposals.mechanism: The secondary gas injection provides additional acceleration to the molten or semi-molten particles after exiting the main combustion chamber, thus further increasing their velocity before impact. This added momentum is expected to boost deposition efficiency, overcome the inadequate thickness observed with the standard HVAF-i7 configuration, and simultaneously maintain coating quality and low oxidation levels.
proposals.predicted_outcome: A significant enhancement in coating thickness and bonding quality relative to the baseline, with the secondary acceleration effectively achieving the deposition rates seen in optimal HVAF-M3 conditions while preserving the necessary oxidation resistance for high-temperature applications.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By focusing solely on improved particle acceleration through a nozzle design change, this intervention offers a single, targeted alteration that directly mitigates the thickness limitation without altering feedstock size, composition, or other processing parameters.

proposals.intervention: Increase the effective deposition power by fine-tuning the fuel-to-gas ratio for improved particle heating and acceleration
proposals.conditions: Adjust the HVAF-i7 fuel and gas mixture to increase combustion energy while keeping the 15–45 μm powder feedstock constant and using a spray distance of 300–350 mm; perform depositions on substrates characteristic of internal diameters as small as 120 mm, under controlled oxidation atmospheres.
proposals.structural_mediator: Enhanced thermal energy input and consequent particle velocities
proposals.mechanism: Modifying the fuel-to-gas ratio will intensify the combustion process, thus raising the particle temperature and velocity. The corresponding increase in kinetic and thermal energy facilitates a more effective flattening and bonding of particles on the substrate, leading to a thicker deposit. This strategy draws on the conventional MCrAlY studies which observed improved deposition efficiency under conditions of heightened particle energy.
proposals.predicted_outcome: The bond coat is anticipated to be thicker and more robust than with the original HVAF-i7 setup, achieving enhanced deposition efficiency while continuing to exhibit minimal oxidation and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This intervention directly counters the thickness limitation by raising the effective deposition energy, thereby improving the kinetic and thermal conditions required for higher deposition efficiency, as supported by analogous improvements seen in the conventional MCrAlY coatings.
